key_insight: A single data-driven closure trained at the expected viscosity can be reused across random-viscosity realizations, with physical constraints improving reduced-order accuracy and robustness.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces the closure-training burden for uncertainty quantification of unsteady incompressible flows with uncertain viscosity.
method: Combine POD reduced-order modeling, spatial filtering, and stochastic collocation.
Train a shared closure using the full-order solution at the expected viscosity.
Compare unconstrained DDC-UQ-ROM with physically constrained CDDC-UQ-ROM.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D cylinder flow with a 5D random viscosity field at mean Re = 100 and 500, including varied correlation lengths and out-of-sample settings, found CDDC-UQ-ROM most accurate and robust for benchmark energy evolution among the compared ROMs.
watch_item: Reusing an expected-viscosity closure may limit accuracy when realization-dependent dynamics differ substantially; validation beyond the tested 2D flows remains necessary.
paper_title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
